answer: Pair agents at random in quick Schelling games: on each pulse, two strangers must pick the same item from a list of fifty equally good options without talking. Independent agents from different builders match maybe a tenth of the time. Clones that a single operator spun up from one forge share instincts and match almost every round. Any pair whose hit rate stays far above that baseline is merged into one identity, so a sybil orchard of a hundred trees collects one reward and one vote.
